divergence_catalog.rustc_1_99_1_behavior: When 5 GPRs (%rdi..%r8) are used and only 1 GPR (%r9) remains (`int_regs == 1`), `u128` spills to stack `8(%rsp), 16(%rsp)` AND leaves `%r9` available for the subsequent `u64` or `Single64` parameter (matching GCC 15.2.0 and System V AMD64 psABI).
divergence_catalog.clang_19_and_cranelift_behavior: `clang-19` (LLVM 19.1.7) and `rustc_codegen_cranelift` (0.1.0) burn/exhaust `%r9` when `i128` spills to the stack, placing the subsequent `u64`/`Single64` parameter on the stack at `24(%rsp)`! Live execution of `rustc_llvm` caller -> `clang-19` or `rustc_cranelift` callee reads garbage from `24(%rsp)` instead of `%r9` (`0x42424242` in `rustc_llvm`/`gcc` vs `0x0` in `clang-19`/`cranelift`).
divergence_catalog.fix_in_rustc_target: In `LeanFnAbiRefinement` (`B7`) and `rustc_codegen_cranelift`, do NOT zero `int_avail` when an `i128`/`u128` argument cannot fit in 1 remaining GPR (`int_avail = 1` is preserved for subsequent 8-byte INTEGER arguments, matching `rustc_llvm 1.99.1` and `gcc 15.2.0`).

divergence_catalog.rustc_1_99_1_behavior: SysV64 & i686: `byval([10 x i8])` on stack (`x86_64.rs:64` checks `offset.is_aligned(field.align.abi)`). Win64: indirect `ptr align 1` in `%rcx`. AAPCS64 (Linux, Darwin, Windows): `Cast([2 x i64])` in `x0, x1` (`aarch64.rs:149-155` ignores internal field unalignment for composites <= 16B).
divergence_catalog.fix_in_rustc_target: Mechanized in `B7`: SysV64 requires per-field alignment check (`hasUnalignedField = false`) for register classification, whereas AAPCS64 classifies any non-HFA composite <= 16B into `[2 x i64]` regardless of packing.

divergence_catalog.signature: u128 register alignment, narrow integer signext/zeroext, tight stack packing, and variadic stack routing
divergence_catalog.rustc_1_99_1_behavior: (1) `fn(u32, u128)`: Linux & WinARM64 even-align `u128` to `x2:x3` (skipping `x1`), whereas Darwin passes `u128` in `x1:x2` (unless wrapped in a 16B-aligned struct `Align16Pair`, which uses `Reg::i128()` in `x2:x3`). (2) Narrow integers (`i8`, `u8`, `i16`, `u16`): Darwin emits caller `signext`/`zeroext` to 32 bits and packs stack arguments at 1/2/4-byte alignment (`f5_darwin_tight_stack_pack` uses `ldrb`/`ldrh`/`ldr` at `[sp]`, `[sp, #2]`, `[sp, #4]`, `[sp, #8]`), whereas Linux/WinARM64 use 8-byte stack slots. (3) Variadics (`...`): Darwin passes all variadic args on the stack; WinARM64 disables FP regs and passes `f64` variadics in GPRs `x1..x7`; Linux AAPCS64 uses both `x0..x7` and `v0..v7`.
divergence_catalog.clang_19_gcc_behavior: 100% agreement between `rustc 1.99.1` and `clang-19` across all three AArch64 targets.

divergence_catalog.signature: fn(SimdF32x4) -> SimdF32x4 and fn(SimdF32x8) -> SimdF32x8 in `extern "Rust"` vs `extern "C"`
divergence_catalog.rustc_1_99_1_behavior: In `extern "Rust"`, `BackendRepr::SimdVector` is ALWAYS `PassMode::Indirect { on_stack: false }` (`ptr align 16/32` and `sret`) so callers with different `-C target-feature` sets remain ABI-compatible. In `extern "C"`, `SimdF32x4` passes in `xmm0`/`v0` (except Win64 `extern "C"` which passes 128-bit vectors by pointer in `%rcx` and returns in `%xmm0`, whereas Win64 `extern "vectorcall"` passes in `%xmm0`). Furthermore, array-backed `#[repr(C)] struct HvaSimd2 { a: SimdF32x4, b: SimdF32x4 }` in Rust is treated as a 32B memory aggregate (>16B `Indirect`) on AArch64 because `SimdF32x4([f32; 4])` has `FieldsShape::Array`, whereas C `struct HvaSimd2` with `__attribute__((vector_size(16)))` is classified by Clang as a 2-element HVA in `q0, q1`!
divergence_catalog.clang_19_gcc_behavior: Clang classifies `struct HvaSimd2` (`2 x __attribute__((vector_size(16)))`) on AArch64 as `[2 x <4 x float>]` in `q0, q1`, whereas `rustc 1.99.1` classifies `HvaSimd2` containing `#[repr(simd)] struct SimdF32x4([f32; 4])` as `Indirect` (`ptr %v`, `sret` in `x8`) because `LayoutData::homogeneous_aggregate` in `compiler/rustc_abi/src/layout.rs` only recurses into `BackendRepr::SimdVector` when it is not wrapped in an array-field struct or when `Reg::vec` matches!
divergence_catalog.fix_in_rustc_target: In `compiler/rustc_abi/src/layout.rs` (`homogeneous_aggregate`), map `BackendRepr::SimdVector { element, count }` of total size 64 or 128 bits to `HomogeneousAggregate::Homogeneous(Reg { kind: RegKind::Vector, size })` so structs of 1..4 `#[repr(simd)]` vectors match Clang's AArch64/vectorcall HVA rule.

divergence_catalog.signature: extern "rust-cold" fn(...) -> ... on 32-bit x86 non-Windows targets
divergence_catalog.rustc_1_99_1_behavior: `compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/abi_map.rs:104-105` maps `ExternAbi::RustCold` to `CanonAbi::Rust` ONLY when `self.os == OsKind::Windows`, leaving `i686-unknown-linux-gnu` as `CanonAbi::RustCold`. Then `compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/abi.rs:723` unconditionally lowers `CanonAbi::RustCold => llvm::PreserveMost` (`preserve_mostcc`), unlike `CanonAbi::RustPreserveNone` (`lines 724-727`) which restricts `PreserveNone` to `Arch::X86_64 | Arch::AArch64`. In LLVM 23.1.1 (`llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86RegisterInfo.cpp`), `CallingConv::PreserveMost` is only supported on 64-bit x86_64 (`!Is64Bit` hits `llvm_unreachable` / null callee-saved register list), causing `rustc +1.99.1 --target i686-unknown-linux-gnu` to die with `SIGSEGV` (`rc = -11`) in `FPPassManager::runOnFunction`!
divergence_catalog.clang_19_gcc_behavior: Clang rejects `__attribute__((preserve_most))` on 32-bit `i686` targets in frontend target sema (`warning: 'preserve_most' calling convention is not supported for this target`).
divergence_catalog.fix_in_rustc_target: In `compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/abi_map.rs:104-105` (and `compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/abi.rs:723`), match `(ExternAbi::RustCold, ArchKind::X86_64 | ArchKind::Aarch64) if self.os != OsKind::Windows => CanonAbi::RustCold` and map all other architectures (including 32-bit `ArchKind::X86`) to `CanonAbi::Rust` (`llvm::CCallConv`).
